about: Where the native roster teardown is intentionally stricter than the recorded Node oracle. Every row is a ruling from the destructive-path review, not an accident.

rows.node: stopAppserver signals the recorded appserver_pid with no sign or identity check, so a row holding -1 signals every process of the user, 0 the process group, and a reused pid an unrelated process
rows.native: only a whole number above 1 and at most 4194304 is ever passed to the signal; its command line must end with `app-server --listen unix://<the member's own socket>` or nothing is signalled, a `appserver pid not verified` warning is given, the result row carries appserver_unverified and the team row stays

rows.where: Ah.Commands TeardownSupport.IsInvokerOrOrchestrator and its use in disband, dismiss
rows.node: the live-peer list of a close can include the session running the command and the orchestrator, so a confirmed close ends the caller's own session
rows.native: the caller's session id, the caller's pane id and any record whose role is orchestrator are left out of every close list (team, no-team peers, single peer), named in a warning; dismiss of such a name is refused

rows.node: the pre-close re-check passes when the pane's current name does not parse or is absent, and resync adopts a pane found by recorded id whatever it is named
rows.native: a member's pane is closed only when it is gone or its current name is the recorded one or another ordinal of the same prefix and role; an unparseable or absent name is refused and the pane stays; resync does not adopt a pane carrying another name

rows.node: tmux kill-pane runs with no timeout
rows.native: tmux kill-pane is bounded at 10 seconds, as list-panes is

rows.node: a name that matches two rows closes or guards the first and then removes every row of that name
rows.native: a name that matches more than one row is refused and nothing changes

rows.node: a pane id from a team file is passed to herdr pane close and tmux kill-pane -t as given
rows.native: a tmux target must be % and digits and a herdr id workspace:pN (an alphanumeric workspace, a colon, p and alphanumerics), or it is not passed on and the row reports it

rows.node: --branch and --base are passed to git worktree add as given, so a value starting with - is read by git as an option
rows.native: a branch that starts with - or fails git check-ref-format --branch, or a base that starts with -, is refused as bad-ref and nothing is written

rows.node: the paste lock file is named from the team id and member name as recorded, so a / or .. in either reaches outside the lock directory
rows.native: a team id or member name outside letters, digits, _, . and - or holding .. is refused (paste: bad_request; deliver: bad-name) before any lock file is made

rows.where: Ah.Launch Paste.PlacementOf, Ah.Commands PaneMembers.TmuxCapture and AnswerVerb cancel
rows.node: a pane id read from a team file is used as the tmux -t target or as a herdr pane as recorded
rows.native: a tmux pane must be % and digits and a herdr pane workspace:pN (a tab id workspace:tN is not a pane), or the member has no addressable pane (deliver: not-sent, answer --cancel: cancel-unsupported) and no multiplexer call is made

rows.where: Ah.Hooks GrantingAnswer, RosterSkillGate (third rule) and AhCliGate, on `roster answer --choice <id>`
rows.node: the answer verb presses the keys of any table row, a granting one (a Yes or an Allow) included; the only guard is the skill's prose that a granting answer goes only on the user's pick, and the allow hook grants every such call prompt-free
rows.native: a `roster answer --choice` whose row grants, or that cannot be shown to name a non-granting row, is asked about on every call (the allow hook stays silent for it, as it does for a close and a trust commit) and is denied in a permission mode where the prompt is not known to reach the user; a non-granting row and `--cancel` stay prompt-free

rows.node: roster.mjs deliver applies no mesh send rule of its own
rows.native: a deliver that is not --wait-only and runs with no CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is refused (exit 2) before anything is sent, because the mesh send rule cannot be applied without the session's identity

rows.where: Ah.Platform AhHomeCheck / PlatformModule.CheckAhHome, enforced in Ah.Cli CliApp.Run (verbs) and HookVerb (hooks)
rows.native: outside test mode an AH_HOME that is not the default home under the passwd entry's home and not listed in the default home's trusted-homes is refused: a verb exits 2 with the recovery text (daemon serve included, so it is not started), a gate denies, an advisory hook is silent with one hook-errors row; where, check, login, home and hook are exempt; an accepted home is its resolved real path
outside test mode the home is the passwd entry's; HOME supplies neither the default state home nor the trust file, and a passwd entry that cannot be read refuses instead of falling back to HOME

rows.where: Ah.Commands RosterCli MutatesTemplate and RefuseRosterEditWhileOwningTeam (roster use, roster copy, roster delete, layout, alias)
rows.node: only init, add, edit and remove were refused while the session owns a live team; roster use, copy, delete, layout and alias ran
rows.native: every verb that writes the roster template is refused with exit 2 and 'edits the roster TEMPLATE, and this session owns live team <id>' while the session owns a live team (0044 section 1.3, applied deliberately; ruled by the Orchestrator on review 1s07)

rows.node: adopt re-stamps only orchestrator.pid and keeps whatever session_id the file already had, so a previous owner's session id stays on a team the adopter now owns
rows.native: adopt sets orchestrator.session_id to the session proven for the adopted pid (a bound daemon registration, or a session-pids row since the process started), and to null when none is proven, adding an `orchestrator session unknown` warning; a stated session id counts only when one of those proofs names it
rows.reason: the mesh gate accepts only a session-id match, and a pid alone confers nothing

doctor.native: `ah <version> at <plugin root>`: the CLI is a native binary and there is no node to name

doctor.node: runs `node --check` on every hooks/*.mjs and reports `every hooks/*.mjs parses` or the files that fail
doctor.native: the row keeps its label and its place in the report; there are no scripts to parse, so it says whether the running ahd matches the plugin manifest it was started with: `ahd <version> is compatible with the plugin at <root> (contract <n>)`, or a warn when no manifest was read
any of the owner, group and other write bits of the directory's mode; the effective-uid check of access(2) is not available to the verb

doctor.node: no such rows: Node has no trust files
doctor.native: one row per trust file: absent, ignored whole with its reason, or its entries each trusted or ignored with the reason; warn when the file or an entry is ignored

doctor.where: Ah.Commands DoctorVerb, row `rebuild-lock`, after the trust rows and before `roster-selection`
doctor.node: no such row: the Node build has no rebuild lock
doctor.native: present only when <home>/bin/.rebuild.lock exists: ok while it is under 10 minutes old, warn when it is older (or has no readable age), naming the file and `rm <file>`; never red, never written
doctor.reason: without flock(1) the install script never takes over a stale lock, and a rebuild started from a hook cannot show its warning
